flags.proposed: Note also the structural check that catches option D instantly: whenever the haircut exceeds the repo interest accrued over the term (here 3.5% against 1%), the repayment must be below the dirty value of the collateral pledged, so an outflow above GBP 9,787,500 signals a dropped haircut.
flags.derivation: Repayment = dirty x (1 - h) x (1 + r t). It exceeds dirty whenever (1-h)(1+rt) > 1, i.e. when the haircut is smaller than the interest accrual; zero- or low-haircut repos on government collateral (e.g. 0-1% haircut, 2% repo for 6 months) repay more than the collateral's dirty value. The 'can never' generalisation is false; the check only works in this question because h = 3.5% > rt = 1%.
